Lat.review: Preserve the source-supported stem and intrinsic pada; inflect for the requested person/number.

Lan.review: Present-system stem plus augment and secondary endings; inspect junctions and final spelling.

Lot.review: Imperative endings/options must be derived for the exact person/number. A printed present singular alone does not certify them.

VidhiLin.review: Ordinary optative formation on the correct stem; verify the exact para/middle ending.

Lit.review: Periphrastic perfect: include licensed auxiliary alternatives, correct auxiliary agreement, and sandhi. Do not mistake multiple gold forms for ambiguous root identity.

Lut.review: Periphrastic future tasi/it formation and person/number endings; preserve lexical vowel quantity.

Lrt.review: sya future with relevant it/aya realization; a correct stem still requires correct endings and sibilant sandhi.

Lrn.review: Conditional future system plus augment and secondary endings.

AshirLin.review: Distinguish the para ni-lopa branch from middle it/retained-aya behavior; do not conflate ordinary optative with benedictive.

Lun.review: Separate intrinsic nic/cang and any explicitly licensed no-nic/sigmatic branches; preserve lexical length and derive augment, reduplication, junctions and endings separately.

3.1.25.use: Curadi nic in the root own meaning is expressly described; this is not an independently requested causative coordinate.

6.4.48.topic: Literal-final-a deletion and its retained conditioning
6.4.48.use: The commentary explicitly uses kathayati to explain why deletion of lexical a does not license ordinary penultimate strengthening.

1.3.74.use: Middle endings depend on the action fruit accruing to the agent; this unspecified context permits relevant alternatives, subject to lexical subgroup restrictions.

1.3.78.use: Parasmaipada applies outside specified Atmanepada conditions. Do not treat every root as freely interchangeable in pada.

3.1.33.use: sya for Lrt/Lrn and tasi for Lut; retain the correct lexical stem and check it/ending realization separately.

3.1.35.use: The relevant derivative base receives am in Lit. A short-root citation does not justify strengthening the inherited lexical stem.

3.1.40.use: The am construction permits kr/bhu/as auxiliaries. Auxiliary agreement and surface sandhi still require task-specific derivation.

6.4.51.topic: Nic loss before an anit ardhadhatuka ending
6.4.51.use: Needed for benedictive/aorist branch distinctions. Compare the explicit para choryat versus middle chorayisista examples in1.3.74 commentary; do not retain or delete aya uniformly.

6.4.71.use: Lan, Lun and Lrn receive the augment under this rule; vowel-initial bases and junctions require their own sandhi analysis.

3.1.48.use: For the nic branch in Kartari Lun, cang replaces cli. An independently licensed no-nic branch must be derived separately.

7.4.2.use: The commentary explicitly discusses kathadi literal-a roots and restriction of the ordinary shortening/reduplicative behavior.

7.4.93.use: The anaglope qualification blocks generic san-like treatment for examples such as acakathat; do not apply a memorized ordinary causative template to all adantas.

7.3.36.use: General puK conditions are distinct from merely lengthening a root vowel. The concrete kathadi alternative is addressed in the separate source finding, not inferred from this rule alone.

7.2.115.topic: Strengthening condition in the reported alternative
7.2.115.use: The Balamonorama passage invokes this strengthening rule when explaining the competing final-a treatment. It does not license p-less kathAyati.
